subject: Tokenizer wave causing intermittent generation failures (UmbrellaSoft)
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena@umbrellasoft.com>, support@umbrellasoft.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tokenizer wave causing intermittent generation failures (UmbrellaSoft)

Hi team,

We're seeing a spike of upstream 5xx/partial responses for requests attributed to UmbrellaSoft over the last ~35 minutes. Root cause appears to be a tokenizer regression introduced in a recent beam/merge that changes how a subset of input sequences are tokenized; the mismatch causes runtime exceptions inside the model runtime for some sequences and results in aborted generation (observed as 502/500 and truncated responses).

What we've done so far:
- Opened an ops bridge and posted a minimal status page update: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/RI-20261113-1
- Rolled traffic off the experimental tokenizer variant back to the stable tokenization path for affected model family in us-west-1 (hotfix completed at 08:58 PT).
- Applied a temporary ingress filter for requests that match the known malformed token pattern to prevent repeated failures.
- Collected an excerpt of the runtime logs and attached a sanitized snippet (incident_log_excerpt.txt).

Customer impact: intermittent generation failures and shortened outputs for ~4% of UmbrellaSoft requests routed to the affected pool between 08:35–09:05 PT. We estimate a roughly 6-minute elevated-error window for most requests due to retries.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can you notify UmbrellaSoft primary contacts (Elena) with a short note that we posted the status page and that we have a mitigation in place? Please include any credits offer language we should apply.
- Olga: can you confirm the rollback is stable across all node pools in the us-west-1 cluster and keep the bridge running until we confirm no recurrence?
- Sean: please capture precise SLO/metric deltas and attach them to the incident ticket (OPS-4921).

I will follow up with a brief postmortem once we have full logs and a root cause analysis.

Thanks,
Mateo
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 17:04:12 -0700
Subject: RE: Tokenizer wave causing intermittent generation failures (UmbrellaSoft) — follow-up and next steps

Quick follow-up now that the bridge is winding down:

Summary:
- Impact window: 2026-11-13T08:35:00-08:58:00 PT (approx). Estimated affected UmbrellaSoft requests: ~1.9k (about 3.8% of traffic for the affected pool).
- Error modes: runtime exception -> 500/502 returned, and in some cases truncated generations where the response ended mid-token. No evidence of persistent data corruption in customer-recorded outputs; truncated generations are visible only in raw response bodies where the client retried or logged incomplete responses.
- Mitigation: rollback to stable tokenizer; ingress filter applied temporarily; monitoring sampling increased by 10x during the window.

Next actions:
- We'll publish a 72-hour postmortem with root cause, timeline, and remediation plan (code revert plus additional unit tests for tokenization edge cases).
- CS (Marissa) to send the brief FYI to UmbrellaSoft and confirm credit issuance.
- Ops (Olga) will leave the rollback in place until end-of-day tomorrow and then coordinate a vetted re-deploy behind a canary with stricter input validation.
- Sean will attach metric deltas to OPS-4921 and share the link; I've linked the ticket above.

I'll assemble a short incident summary we can both publish to the status page and share with UmbrellaSoft. Thanks everyone for the rapid turnaround.

Mateo
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
